text: The Board of Trustees of Galveston Wharves urges that the port of Galveston be included in the Houston commercial zone. It points out that the proposed expanded Houston zone would include nearly all of Galveston County, but not the city of Galveston. The Houston Port Bureau and the Houston Chamber of Commerce, however, support the proposed expanded zone which does not include Galveston. The Greater Baton Rouge Port Commission suggests that the proposal be amended to allow application of the maximum radius authorized for any city under the population-mileage formula to determine terminal areas at port cities for traffic having a prior or subsequent movement by water, regardless of the population of the port city. This would create uniform terminal areas at all port cities and equalize the competitive balance between the ports of large and small cities. The Port Everglades Authority suggests the establishment of seaport commercial zones for shipments in foreign commerce having a prior or subsequent movement by water. It recommends that these zones be equal to three times the distance of any mileage formula established for the commercial zone of the seaport city. It also urges the Commission to adopt a procedure that will enable a city which is built adjacent to a physical barrier to add territory to its commercial zone which is equal to the territory excluded from the zone due to the physical barrier. The Port of Bremerton urges that the proposed Seattle zone be further expanded to include an airport and an industrial park which would be just outside the new Seattle zone.
